To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the C(8) aryl adducts of the purine bases adenine and guanines are readily synthesized in good yields via reaction of a di- or trisubstituted aniline with the corresponding aldehyde, which is readily prepared by reaction of the corresponding PAH (e.g., benzo[a]anthracenes) with a 1,3-diamine or triamine precursor.

the synthesis of C(8) adducts of purine nucleosides with carcinogenic PAH radical cation metabolite involves a simple and efficient approach, which entails direct reaction of PAH aldehydes with di- or triamines, and that the C(8) adenine and guanines adducts of BP and DBC were prepared by this method in good yield.

efficient syntheses of the C(9)-aryl adduct of 8-oxoguanine (6-BP-C8-Oxogua) and of the C(10)-aryl adduct 8,9-dihydro-10-(deoxyribosyl)guanine (10-DBC-C8-Gua) derived from carcinogenic polycylic aromatic hydrocarbons, such as dibenzo[ def,p]chrysine, have been developed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of the C-8-aryl adducts that are formed by reaction of carcinogenic polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons and their metabolites with DNA.
the efficient synthesis of the C8-purine adducts that are formed by reaction of PAH radical cation metabolite intermediates with DNA.
the development of efficient syntheses of C8-purine adducts formed by reaction of DNA with the radical cation (and possibly other) metabolites of carcinogen PAHs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C(8) aryl adducts of purine bases and nucleosides derived from PAHs can be readily prepared in moderate to good yields via direct reaction of PAH aldehydes with di- or triamines.
the C(8) aryl adducts of the adenine and guanines derived from the carcinogenic PAH BP and DBC, and from other PAHs, are readily synthesized by the method reported here.
the Suzuki-Miyaura approach to the C(8) adducts of purine bases with aryl groups is a useful method, but the scope of this method is limited.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method for the synthesis of the C-8 adducts of DNA with PAHs.

the C(8) aryl adducts of purines formed by reaction of PAH radical cation metabolite with DNA can be synthesized in good yields via direct reaction of a short-lived PAH aldehyde intermediate with a di- and triamine precursor of the purine.

the C(8) adducts of the carcinogenic PAH radical cation metabolite with adenine and guanosine are readily accessible by the direct reaction of the PAH aldehyde precursor with a di- (or tri-) amino derivative of adenine or guanine, and the method is superior to the existing methods for the synthesis of these important DNA adducts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthesis of C(8) adducts of purine bases and nucleosides is now a straightforward process that is amenable to the preparation of a variety of C(8)-(aryl) adducts.

the direct aldehyde addition method is a superior synthetic method for the preparation of C(8) adducts of the carcinogenic PAH radical cation metabolite-DNA adducts, such as those of 6-BP, 10-DBC, 6-BaP, and 10-DCB.

direct reaction of a short-lived PAH aldehyde intermediate with a di- (or tri)amine precursor of a nucleoside provides a convenient, efficient, and general method for the synthesis of the C-8 adducts of the purine bases of DNA with PAHs.
